description: The WHEN DFHPF3 arm of the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :184-195 - the second of its exactly three arms, and the second of this folder's two gate G40 cases. The unit is ReportRequestController constructed as a plain Java object with mainPara called as an ordinary method: no MockMvc, no servlet container, no session (unitKind CONTROLLER_POJO, gate G51). CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as '1', which is 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, so :177 takes its ELSE and :183 PERFORM RECEIVE-TRNRPT-SCREEN runs before any key is examined. EVALUATE is ordered and the first match wins (gate G30): WHEN DFHENTER at :185 is tested first and does not match, WHEN DFHPF3 at :187 matches, and WHEN OTHER at :190 is last and is never reached - which is why this case pins no CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY text. All ten unprotected xxxI items of the seventeen app/cpy-bms/CORPT00.CPY declares are supplied at their declared widths and together form a complete, armed custom-range submission; not one of them is inspected on this arm, and pinning them is what proves it, because a translation that consulted the map here would still satisfy a case that left it blank. CORPT00C copies neither CSSTRPFY nor CSSETATY - it tests EIBAID inline - so the AID is declared as the DFHAID mnemonic DFHPF3 and folded through common.PfKeyResolver onto PFK03, whose boolean outcome the inline test must agree with; DFHAID and DFHBMSCA are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, so common.CicsAid is the single reproduction of the 0xF3 byte (risk R-D). :188 moves 'COMEN01C' into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM and :189 performs RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN, where the guard at :542 is FALSE because :188 has already set the target - that redundant guard and the inline EIBAID test are both preserved exactly as the source has them (practice B5) - and then :545-547 move WS-TRANID 'CR00' (:38) into CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, WS-PGMNAME 'CORPT00C' (:37) into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM and ZEROS into CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT before the XCTL at :549. Gate G40: nextProgram is exactly the eight characters COMEN01C, resolved by the client, with no server-side forward. Gate G37 and rule R6: the whole 160-byte communication area travels in the payload and nowhere else, the REENTER flag is deliberately reset to '0' on the way out, and all sixteen COCOM01Y fields are written out so that the twelve which pass through unchanged are observable rather than assumed (practice B8). Nothing is sent - no SEND means sends is empty, no mapset or map is named and no cursor is requested - and nothing is written either, because no EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD runs, so the JOBS job-submission port that app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:499-505 defines as RECORDSIZE(80) RECORDFORMAT(FIXED) DISPOSITION(MOD) has no rows and neither expectedWrites nor expectedDatasets carries an entry. NO THANK-YOU LITERAL IS EMITTED, and that is a deliberate correction rather than an omission: many CardDemo programs emit one on the PF3 exit but CORPT00C does not, and exhaustive search shows the only CCDA-* references in the whole program are CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY at :193, CCDA-TITLE01 at :613 and CCDA-TITLE02 at :614. The two candidate literals genuinely differ and must never be conflated: app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:23-24 declares CCDA-THANK-YOU PIC X(40) as 'Thank you for using CCDA application... ', forty characters naming CCDA, while app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:18-19 declares CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU PIC X(50) as 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...' padded to fifty, naming CardDemo - different text and different width. Neither appears anywhere in CORPT00C, so neither appears here. The two emitted lines are consequently both blank: WS-MESSAGE keeps the eighty spaces :169 moved into it and ERRMSGO the seventy-eight spaces :170 moved into it, reported on separate channels because MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :560 loses two bytes on the right and a single channel could not show that. There is no DISPLAY_LINE entry - DISPLAY 'PROCESS ENTER KEY' at :210 sits inside PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, which this arm never enters - and expectedReturnCode is 0 because CORPT00C sets no RETURN-CODE and contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD'. Two instructions for this case could not be honoured literally, and they are recorded here rather than absorbed (practice B12). First, an empty expectedMessages list is not expressible: the adapter records the WS_MESSAGE_80 and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channels on every path and FieldDiffer compares the count before the text, so an empty list would raise MESSAGE_COUNT_MISMATCH and fail the very diff-count-zero gate G18 it was asked to satisfy - two all-blank entries carry the same fact correctly, and the requirement they exist for, that no thank-you line and no DISPLAY line is claimed, is met exactly. Second, separate pinned date and time members do not exist: ParityCase declares one ISO-8601 pinnedClock, which here keeps the folder-wide 2022-07-19T23:12:34 the other nineteen cases pin, is never read on this arm because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO is not reached, and is pinned only for determinism (practice B7). Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/CORPT00.CPY and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD, whose :409-410 binds transaction CR00 to this program - never captured from a live COBOL execution, which eight verified environment blockers make impossible here (risk R-A). review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', so no user rule governs this fixture; that absence is not licence to lower the bar, and the plan's own practices are held instead - B1, because every one of the sixteen commarea fields and ten screen fields carries a real value and nothing is a placeholder; B3, because app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd, app/jcl and app/proc are read-only reference and were not touched; and B8, because the code page is named US-ASCII and never left to the platform default.
